- [IARC.1.15] **Compiled artefacts are bytes libds owns;
  cross-process surfaces are not.** The "no wire, no
  protocol" stance ([IARC.1.14]) governs **runtime
  interactions across libds's process boundary** —
  telemetry, action dispatch, fact assertion from the
  outside, debug subscription, peer bridging. The DS
  compiler artefact (`.dsc`, specified at [RDSC]) is a different category: it is a
  one-way compiler-to-runtime artefact loaded once at
  engine setup, not a continuing communication channel.
  libds owns its decoder (protobuf-c per
  [IARC.7.4]) the same way it owns the Rete network —
  internal machinery, not a surface.
  This narrowly authorises libds to read structured
  bytes from disk while preserving the invariant that
  every **runtime** boundary remains a typed C
  callback. libds **must not** use the DSC dependency
  (protobuf-c) for any other purpose: wire
  encoding for cross-engine bridging, telemetry
  serialisation, debug protocol, peer transport.
  Schema-typed cross-boundary serialisation by the
  integrator (each schema has a generated `.proto`
  shipped inside the artefact per
  [LFAC.8] and
  [RDSC.5.8]) is
  enabled by the artefact, not performed by libds: the
  integrator who wants to encode a fact reads the
  schema's `.proto` from the loaded engine and runs
  their own protobuf encoder. libds supplies the
  shape; the integrator owns the bytes.
